policy: A wrapper is not removed merely because its target exists. Removal requires all consumers to be migrated first.

wrappers.detail: calculateCampaignPreview() and validateCampaignPricing() delegate to PricingEngine, but the class also retains genuine request-reconciliation logic that is NOT a pass-through. Treating it as a pure wrapper would misdescribe it.
wrappers.current_consumers: 131 inbound references - the widest fan-in in the codebase.
wrappers.reason_it_exists: Created in Phase 0.6 so existing callers could be migrated to the engine without touching call sites; it also insulates callers from the engine's request shape.
wrappers.can_consumers_migrate_safely: Not safely in this phase. 131 call sites span controllers, services and the campaign booking use case, and the reconciliation logic has no other home.
wrappers.deletion_condition: When the reconciliation logic is extracted into a named Application-layer use case AND all 131 consumers are migrated. That is a multi-phase effort, not a retirement.

wrappers.detail: calculatePreview() returns $this->legacyEngine->calculatePreview($params) verbatim. Constructor-injects the concrete PricingEngine.
wrappers.reason_it_exists: Introduced in an earlier phase to isolate and preserve legacy multi-asset pricing behaviour for the V2 endpoint without duplicating the algorithm.
wrappers.can_consumers_migrate_safely: Only by changing the V2 pricing contract, which is prohibited.
wrappers.deletion_condition: When /api/v2/pricing/calculate is retired or re-specified. Retained.

note: Both wrappers are load-bearing. Neither was removed, which is the correct outcome: the brief forbids deleting a wrapper just because the target exists.
